_comment: Image -> 3D GAUSSIAN SPLAT with TripoSplat, plus a rendered orbit turntable video and a .spz file. TripoSplat beat Hunyuan3D 2.1 in human-preference tests (Elo 1137 vs 996) and is a tenth the download - but it outputs splats, not meshes. Use workflow 24 when you need geometry a game engine can eat.
_notes: The turntable is the point. RenderSplat with frames=90 and an orbit camera produces a full 360 turn, which CreateVideo turns into an MP4. That single output communicates a 3D result better than any still, and it is the reason this workflow is worth running even when you also make a mesh.

BiRefNet runs FIRST (nodes 3-6) to matte the subject, and TripoSplatPreprocessImage takes both the image AND the mask. A splat built from an un-matted image reconstructs the background as a cloud of floating gaussians around your subject. Do not skip it. Note the mask handed to TripoSplatPreprocessImage is the FOREGROUND mask straight from RemoveBackground - no InvertMask here, unlike the RGBA path in workflow 14.
CreateCameraInfo.mode is a dynamic combo, so its sub-inputs are DOTTED: `mode.yaw`, `mode.pitch`, `mode.distance`. See workflow 15's notes on COMFY_DYNAMICCOMBO_V3.

pitch 20 looks better than the template's 30 for most objects - a slightly lower orbit reads as a product turntable rather than a drone shot. distance 2.5 frames a unit-scale object tightly; raise it if the subject clips the frame edges.
num_gaussians 262144 is the density. It is the main quality/VRAM dial. 131072 halves memory with a visible but acceptable softening.

Three outputs on purpose: the orbit MP4 (for looking at), the .spz splat file (Niantic gzip format, ~10x smaller than .ply, base colour only - the deliverable), and a mesh converted via SplatToMesh (a convenience, noticeably worse than Hunyuan3D's - do not use it as your mesh path).
render_style also accepts `clay`, `depth` and `normal`. `clay` is genuinely useful for judging geometry without colour hiding defects.
dino_v3_vit_h is the vision encoder here, NOT the sigclip used elsewhere, and flux2-vae does double duty as the image VAE - that is why TripoSplat is only ~2.8 GB on top of what you already had.
